rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjunctive لا introduces a new negation; it cannot be used to carve out an item already included in a general negation, for which و لا is required.
rows.anchor: وهي موضوعة لأن تنفي بها ما بدأت ، فأوجبته لا لأن تفيد بها النفي في شيء قد نفيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ما جاءني إلا زيد, the wording has already explicitly negated arrival by everyone else, so adding لا عمرو repeats a negation already made.
rows.anchor: فقد نفيت أن يكون قد جاءك أحد غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنما جاءني زيد and زيد هو الجائي assert a particular arrival positively; excluding others follows by implication, not an expressed negation, so لا عمرو may follow.
rows.anchor: وهو كلام كما تراه مثبت ليس فيه نفي البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual order is to put the object before إلا: ما ضرب زيدا إلا عمرو, restricting the agent to striking Zayd.
rows.anchor: وإنما الأكثر أن تقدم المفعول على ' إلا ' ، نحو : ما ضرب زيدا إلا عمر و

rows.speaker: هم
rows.claim: Some analyze ما ضرب إلا عمرو زيدا as two clauses, with زيدا governed by an omitted verb after the initial statement.
rows.anchor: وأن زيدا منصوب بفعل مضمر ، حتى كأن المتكلم بذلك أبهم في أول أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To restrict عمرو specifically to striking Zayd, the speaker must state the object first; without it, listeners infer that only عمرو struck at all and that every victim was struck by him.
rows.anchor: حتى تكون قد بدأت فعديته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Words signify meanings and can disclose them as they are; a sign cannot itself transform the meaning or give it a quality it did not have.
rows.anchor: الألفاظ أدلة على المعاني ، وليس للدليل إلا أن يعلمك الشيء على ما يكون عليه

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: The familiar rule says that whoever takes a bare meaning and clothes it in wording of his own becomes more entitled to it.
rows.anchor: قول العلماء حيث ذكروا الأخذ والسرقة : إن من أخذ معنى عاريا فكساه لفظا من عنده كان أحق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurjani challenges the rule: a meaning cannot be bare of words, and if the borrower adds no quality or merit, new wording alone cannot make it his.
rows.anchor: من أين يتصور أن يكون هاهنا معنى عار من لفظ يدل عليه ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clothing a meaning must mean giving it a new form; treating metaphor as merely substituting a word cannot explain added merit or a stronger claim to the meaning.
rows.anchor: والاستعارة عندكم مقصورة على مجرد اللفظ ، ولا ترون المستعير يصنع بالمعنى شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an example of reworking an existing meaning, Jurjani introduces Abu Tammam's verse based on a line by Abu Nukhayla.
rows.anchor: فإن من أحسن شيء فيه ما صنع أبو تمام في بيت أبي نخيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما ضربت إلا زيدا is sound, but fronting أنا after negation in ما أنا ضربت إلا زيدا makes the denial conflict with إلا, which asserts that the speaker did strike Zayd.
rows.anchor: لأن نقض النفي بإلا يقتضي أن تكون ضربت زيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the verb first, ما ضربت زيدا denies that the speaker struck Zayd but leaves other objects open; with the object first, ما زيدا ضربت presupposes a strike and denies only that Zayd was its object.
rows.anchor: فإذا قلت : ما ضربت زيدا ؛ فقدمت الفعل كان المعنى أنك قد نفيت أن يكون قد وقع ضرب منك على زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verb-focused negation can be followed by an opposite action; object-focused negation instead needs another object as contrast, and fronted prepositional complements work the same way.
rows.anchor: ما ضربت زيدا ولكني أكرمته

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان الجاحظ
rows.claim: Al-Jahiz recounts Qays ibn Kharija's long settlement speech, in which he expansively urged reconciliation and prohibited division.
rows.anchor: ذكره أبو عثمان الجاحظ في كتاب البيان والتبيين

rows.speaker: أبو يعقوب
rows.claim: Abu Yaqub explains that allusion and indirect expression do not affect the mind as directly as explicit explanation and disclosure.
rows.anchor: فقيل لأبي يعقوب : هلا اكتفى بالأمر بالتواصل ، عن النهي عن التقاطع ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explicitly naming the central object of negation has a force that a pronoun lacks; in Dhu al-Rumma's line, denying praise of the miser is primary and appeasement is only its rationale.
rows.anchor: إيقاع نفي المدح على اللئيم صريحا ، والمجيء به مكشوفا ظاهرا هو الواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the explicit wording in the Qur'anic examples gives beauty, grandeur, and nobility that would be lost by replacing the repeated phrase with a pronoun.
rows.anchor: للتصريح عملا لا يكون مثل ذلك العمل للكناية كان لإعادة اللفظ في مثل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Atahiya's image of praise opened by virtues parallels Abu Tammam's image of gifts stringing praise like pearls for an inarticulate tongue.
rows.anchor: قول أبي العتاهية ، + الخفيف + : ( شيم فتحت من المدح ما قد كان مستغلقا على المداح )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Wajza and Mansur al-Namri both picture generosity as streams or valleys converging at the praised man.
rows.anchor: قول أبي وجزة ، + الوافر + : ( أتاك المجد من هنا وهنا وكنت له كمجتمع السيول )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashshar's hated gray hair that one hates to lose is echoed by al-Buhturi's complaint that beauties criticize his gray hair, which he cannot enjoy as a flaw.
rows.anchor: قول بشار ، + البسيط + : ( الشيب كره وكره أن يفارقني أعجب بشيء على البغضاء مودود )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Tammam makes tomorrow long for the perfected man and yesterday yearn toward him; Ibn al-Rumi's distinctive image is a grieving glance from yesterday working toward him.
rows.anchor: وقول أبي تمام ، + الوافر + : ( يشتاقه من كماله غده ويكثر الوجد نحوه الأمس )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Tammam says wolves and vultures cannot repay the morning's benefit; al-Mutanabbi recasts the image as beasts of prey praising the benefactor's generosity.
rows.anchor: وقول أبي تمام ، + الطويل + : ( لئن ذمت الأعداء سوء صباحها فليس يؤدي شكرها الذئب والنسر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Tammam contrasts souls close despite distance and bodies near yet estranged; al-Mutanabbi pictures hearts meeting in bodies that do not meet.
rows.anchor: وقول أبي تمام ، + البسيط + : ( ورب نائي المغاني روحه أبدا لصيق روحي ، ودان ليس بالداني )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Haffan says the age is wholly harmful except for Ibn Yahya, its one grace; al-Mutanabbi depicts days relieved of blame as though their children were guilty and the addressee their excuse.
rows.anchor: وقول أبي هفان ، + الرمل + : ( أصبح الدهر مسيئا كله ما له إلا ابن يحيى حسنه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali ibn Jabala says nights return lost strength as wisdom and understanding; Ibn al-Mu'tazz says lost youth increases men's judgment and intellect.
rows.anchor: وقول علي بن جبلة ، + الكامل + : ( وأرى الليالي ما طوت من قوتي ردته في عظتي وفي إفهامي )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examining Qur'anic passages verse by verse reveals no misplaced or inferior word, but an order and precision that dazzle minds, defeat the public, and silence eloquent challengers.
rows.anchor: فلم يجدوا في الجميع كلمة ينبو بها مكانها ، ولفظة ينكر شأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted poem criticizes people who make claims without understanding them and cannot substantiate them when challenged.
rows.anchor: يقولون أقوالا ولا يعلمونها ولو قيل : هاتوا حققوا لم يحققوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A student should investigate the Qur'an's stylistic qualities and why its effects exceed human capacity instead of merely memorizing the apparent wording of proofs.
rows.anchor: أأن يقلد في ذلك ، ويحفظ متن الدليل وظاهر لفظه ولا يبحث عن تفسير المزايا والخصائص ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The way to understand these qualities is to examine Arabic speech and poetry comprehensively, tracing each topic with evidence and examples.
rows.anchor: استقراء كلام العرب وتتبع أشعارهم ، والنظر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary speakers understand one another's purposes necessarily; understanding a sentence's meaning therefore requires no extra evidence beyond its wording.
rows.anchor: أجمع العقلاء على أن العلم بمقاصد الناس في محاوراتهم علم ضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sign must inform its hearer of what it signifies, and conversation aims to disclose the speaker's purpose; otherwise the proposed meaning would not be conveyed by the words.
rows.anchor: الدلالة على الشيء هي لا محالة إعلامك السامع إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a report merely communicated that its predicate exists in its subject, a polytheist asserting another god would intend to teach that such a god exists, exposing the theory's absurdity.
rows.anchor: فالكافر إذا أثبت مع الله - تعالى عما يقول الظالمون - إلها آخر يكون قاصدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rival account would make every heard report certainly true, despite reports admitting falsehood; it would also erase the distinction between solitary and mass-transmitted reports and remove the need for miracles.
rows.anchor: وهو يقتضي أن يكون الخبر على وفق المخبر عنه أبدا ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abbas ibn al-Ahnaf aptly uses pouring tears as a sign of grief, since crying conventionally signals sorrow, as do the idioms and the cited line about time making one cry or laugh.
rows.anchor: إلى قول العباس بن الأحنف ، من + الطويل + : ( سأطلب بعد الدار عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem's wish that the eyes become dry cannot signal reunion's joy: الجمود means an eye fails to weep when grief calls for tears, so the condition is a defect and complaint.
rows.anchor: ألا إن عينا لم تجد يوم واسط عليك بجاري دمعها لجمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The language calls an eye without tears, a year without rain, and a she-camel without milk جماد, each suggesting withholding or barrenness rather than happiness.
rows.anchor: عين جمود ؛ لا ماء فيها ، وسنة جماد ؛ لا مطر فيها ، وناقة جماد ؛ لا لبن فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person can be eager only for what is not yet present; desire cannot properly target what already exists or what is past.
rows.anchor: وإنما يكون الحرص على ما لم يوجد بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life is indefinite in لكم في القصاص حياة because the point is life gained for some future portion through deterrence, not life itself or life in every period; the same partial benefit explains فيه شفاء للناس.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان المعنى على حياة في بعض أوقاته وجب التنكير ، وامتنع التعريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person deterred from murder is not the one whose life is saved by qisas; qisas saves the intended victim who otherwise would be killed, further restricting the meaning to a subset.
rows.anchor: هذه الحياة إنما هي لمن كان يقتل لولا القصاص

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: An unattributed verse assigns gifts across the lands of Najd and the lowlands to one generous benefactor.
rows.anchor: ففي كل نجد في البلاد وغائر مواهب ليست منه وهي مواهبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutanabbi's inaccessible beloved who entices beneath her veil is paired with al-Buhturi's woman who arouses hope, then turns away and disappoints.
rows.anchor: قول المتنبي ، + البسيط + : ( بيضاء تطمع فيما تحت حلتها وعز ذلك مطلوبا إذا طلبا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutanabbi's wish to be remembered by one who will not translate his desire parallels Abu Tammam's paradox of gaining glory by forgoing pursuit.
rows.anchor: وقول المتنبي ، + الكامل + : ( إذكار مثلك ترك إذكاري له إذ لا تريد لما أريد مترجما )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutanabbi's sunlike woman appears when veiled, echoing Qays ibn al-Khatim's wish that God made her impossible to veil.
rows.anchor: وقول أبي تمام ، + الكامل + : ( فنعمت من شمس إذا حجبت بدت من خدرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutanabbi's eyelashes wound hearts before skin, paralleling Kathir's arrow-like glance that leaves the skin untouched but wounds the heart.
rows.anchor: وقول المتنبي ، + الخفيف + : ( راميات بأسهم ريشها الهدب تشق القلوب قبل الجلود )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verse attributed to Labid makes safety itself a disease, while Abu al-Atahiya says a person's perfection hastens his decline.
rows.anchor: ويعزى إلى لبيد ، + الكامل + : ( ودعوت ربي بالسلامة جاهدا ليصحني فإذا السلامة داء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Atahiya says a lover's visits should be reduced so affection stays fresh; Abu Tammam similarly says a long stay wears one down and travel renews.
rows.anchor: وقوله ، + مجزوء الكامل + : ( أقلل زيارتك الحبيب تكون كالثوب استجده )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khuraymi says his benefactor underestimates a kindness celebrated by others; al-Mutanabbi says people mistake the addressee's absence for their own good fortune.
rows.anchor: وقول الخريمي ، + الرمل + : ( زاد معروفك عندي عظما أنه عندك محقور صغير )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Buhturi observes that calamities target people of virtue; al-Mutanabbi similarly says the age targets the best people, leaving the least perceptive free of worry.
rows.anchor: وقول البحتري ، + الوافر + : ( ألم تر للنوائب كيف تسمو إلى أهل النوافل والفضول ؟ )
